hook.convey: closed shape → walk its edge from one corner, all the way back to the same corner → how far = perimeter; fence round a field, lace along a dupatta edge, rope round a ground
hook.slotUse: the closed shape whose edge is walked, laced or bordered; its sides supply the lengths to add

explain.convey: perimeter (parimap) = total length of the boundary of a closed shape → start at a corner, go along every side, end at the start corner; triangle 4 cm, 5 cm, 6 cm → 4 + 5 + 6 = 15 cm
explain.point: the trace going round the triangle over its three labelled sides 4 cm, 5 cm and 6 cm, back to the start corner

explain.convey: any polygon (bahubhuj) → same rule: add every side, however many; hexagon = 6 sides → 6 lengths in the sum; a side with no label still belongs to the boundary → still added
explain.point: the six sides AB, BC, CD, DE, EF, FA, taken one after another from corner A back to A

explain.convey: perimeter = AROUND the shape (string on the edge) → a length → cm, m, km; area = INSIDE (tiles covering the surface) → a different quantity; 6 cm by 4 cm card → edge = 6 + 4 + 6 + 4 = 20 cm, not 6 × 4
explain.point: the traced edge of the rectangle: top 6 cm, right 4 cm, bottom 6 cm, left 4 cm, versus the empty inside

workedExample.problem: A five-sided flower bed has sides 4 m, 5 m, 3 m, 6 m and 2 m. How much fencing goes once around it?
givens: the flower bed is a closed five-sided shape (pentagon)
sides: 4 m, 5 m, 3 m, 6 m, 2 m
workedExample.find: the perimeter of the flower bed (fencing needed once around)

steps.do: fencing goes along the boundary → perimeter = sum of all sides
add the fifth side → all 5 sides used, back at the start corner

workedExample.why: fence runs along the edge → perimeter; 5 sides → 5 lengths in the sum, none left out; answer is a length → m, not square m

checks.prompt: An L-shaped room has 6 sides. Going round from one corner, the sides are 8 m, 3 m, 5 m, 4 m, 3 m and 7 m. What is the perimeter of the room?
A card has sides 10 cm, 4 cm, 10 cm and 4 cm going round. How much lace is needed to go once around its edge?

ladder.why: first straight use: triangle, three given sides → add all
decide perimeter vs area from the situation: lace around vs cloth covering
error-spot: Riya stops at 5 of 6 sides of an L-shape → find the left-out side and the true perimeter
six unequal edges in a real context (exhibition board tape) → every edge, once

remediation.move: named-corner walk instead of a list of numbers: start at A, write each side's name as its length goes into the sum (AB, BC, … FA); sum is done only when the walk is back at A
remediation.then: A 6-sided field ABCDEF has AB = 10 m, BC = 4 m, CD = 6 m, DE = 5 m, EF = 4 m and FA = 9 m. What is its perimeter?

remediation.move: string vs tiles: string laid along the edge then straightened against a ruler = perimeter (cm); tiles laid inside = area; perimeter question → string, so add the edge lengths, never multiply them
remediation.then: Ribbon goes once around the edge of a label 5 cm long and 3 cm wide. How long is the ribbon?

skills.bridgeToNext: adding every side always works → rectangle: sides come in equal pairs (lambai, chaudai, lambai, chaudai) → shortcut 2 × (l + b); square: 4 equal sides → 4 × side

hook.convey: rectangle and square boundaries everywhere → a quicker way than writing 4 numbers each time, because sides repeat
hook.slotUse: the rectangular or square thing whose edge is measured; it supplies the length and breadth (or side)

explain.convey: rectangle (aayat) → opposite sides equal → going round: lambai, chaudai, lambai, chaudai → 10 + 6 + 10 + 6 = 32 m
explain.point: the two 10 m lengths (top and bottom) and the two 6 m breadths (left and right)

explain.convey: one length + one breadth = corner to opposite corner = HALF the way round; full round = that half twice → P = 2 × (l + b) = 2 × (10 + 6) = 2 × 16 = 32 m; l + b alone = 16 m = only half the boundary
explain.point: the trace from the bottom-left corner along the 10 m length and up the 6 m breadth to the opposite corner, then the second half back

explain.convey: square (varg) → all 4 sides equal → 6 + 6 + 6 + 6 = 4 × 6 = 24 cm → P = 4 × side; answer is a length → cm, not square cm
explain.point: the four equal 6 cm sides of the square

workedExample.problem: A rectangular notebook cover is 24 cm long and 18 cm wide. How much tape goes once around its edge?
workedExample.find: the perimeter of the cover (tape needed once around the edge)

steps.do: tape goes along the edge → perimeter; rectangle sides go l, b, l, b → P = 2 × (l + b)
bracket first: one length + one breadth = half the edge
double the half to get the full edge
cross-check by adding all four sides

workedExample.why: rectangle edge = two lengths + two breadths → (l + b) taken twice; 42 cm alone is half the edge; 24 × 18 = 432 would be area (inside), not the edge

checks.prompt: A rectangular playground is 40 m long and 25 m wide. What is its perimeter?
Lace is sewn once around the edge of a rectangular table mat 9 cm long and 5 cm wide. How much lace is needed?
A square tile has side 11 cm. What is its perimeter?

ladder.why: direct 2 × (l + b) on a small rectangle, 8 cm by 5 cm
direct 4 × side on a square, in metres
error-spot: Raj's 19 m for a 12 m by 7 m garden = l + b once → name the missing two sides, give 38 m
explain the formula itself: why (l + b) is taken twice
both formulas side by side (square rangoli vs rectangular mat) → compare, spot equal perimeters

remediation.move: ant walk with a running counter instead of a formula: ant starts at a corner, counter after each side 14 → 20 → 34 → 40 m; l + b = 20 m = ant only at the opposite corner, halfway; sides walked 4, sides added in l + b only 2
remediation.then: An ant walks once round a rectangular field 20 m long and 9 m wide. What does its distance counter show at the end?

remediation.move: string around vs tiles inside the same rectangle: string along the edge → straightened on a ruler → cm (perimeter); tiles covering → square cm (area); 7 × 3 counts tiles, not string
remediation.then: String goes once around the edge of a bookmark 8 cm long and 2 cm wide. How long is the string?

skills.bridgeToNext: formula forward: sides → perimeter; real problems run it backward and onward: square side = P ÷ 4; rectangle P ÷ 2 = l + b → breadth = P ÷ 2 − l; perimeter × rate per metre → fencing cost; perimeter × rounds → distance run

hook.convey: real boundary jobs → perimeter is the first number, then one more step: rounds × perimeter, metres × rate, or perimeter back to a side
hook.slotUse: the real ground being run round, fenced or marked, plus the rounds, the price per metre, or the known perimeter

explain.convey: backward for a square: perimeter 60 m shared by 4 equal sides → side = 60 ÷ 4 = 15 m; check: 4 × 15 = 60 m
explain.point: the four equal 15 m sides that together make the 60 m boundary

explain.convey: backward for a rectangle: perimeter 60 m, length 20 m → half the perimeter = one length + one breadth = 30 m → breadth = 30 − 20 = 10 m; check: 2 × (20 + 10) = 60 m
explain.point: one 20 m length plus one 10 m breadth = half of the traced boundary

explain.convey: fencing cost = perimeter (m) × rate (₹ per m); 12 m by 8 m plot → 2 × (12 + 8) = 40 m → at ₹10 per m → 40 × 10 = ₹400; a gate or gap with no wire → subtract its length from the perimeter before multiplying
explain.point: the traced fence line all around the 12 m by 8 m rectangle

workedExample.problem: Rani runs 3 rounds of a rectangular park 50 m long and 30 m wide. How far does she run?

steps.do: one round = once along the whole boundary → perimeter of the park

workedExample.why: each round covers the whole boundary once = 160 m; 3 equal rounds → multiply by 3; 3 × (50 + 30) = 240 m would be only half a round each time

checks.prompt: A square garden has a perimeter of 84 m. How long is one side?

ladder.why: backward for a square: perimeter 400 m → one side
backward for a rectangle: perimeter and length known → halve, then subtract the length
fencing cost: perimeter × ₹ per metre, then the gate variant → subtract 2 m before multiplying

remediation.move: ant walk run backward: full boundary = 2 lengths + 2 breadths; ant at the opposite corner = half the perimeter = 1 length + 1 breadth; 18 m by 12 m → 60 m round, half = 30 m = 18 + 12 → so halve the perimeter first, then take away the length
remediation.then: A rectangular pond has a perimeter of 80 m and a length of 25 m. What is its breadth?

remediation.move: wire is bought by the metre of edge, not by the ground inside: string around the plot vs tiles inside it; cost = edge length (m) × ₹ per m; l × b = ground covered, not wire
remediation.then: Wire costing ₹20 per metre goes once around a plot 10 m long and 6 m wide. What does the wire cost?
